title: Elliptic curve traits and their security connections
one_liner: All 22 DiSSECT traits and eight foundations, with factorization explained and a six-phase study plan.
description: Trace, CM discriminants, j-invariants, torsion and isogenies: what elliptic curve traits mean for cryptographic security.
standfirst: A curve’s properties answer different questions. Some constrain discrete-logarithm security, some describe endomorphisms and isogenies, and others expose implementation or generation choices. This guide connects them without collapsing them into a single score.

facts.Coverage: 22 published DiSSECT traits plus eight foundational quantities
facts.Scope: Educational interpretation, not a completed security evaluation
facts.Example: Recomputed from a small curve by the site build

blocks.p: DiSSECT's AFRICACRYPT 2022 paper reports 22 traits, all listed in Appendix A. Sedláček's thesis, Appendix F.1, contains the same 22 entries with nonconsecutive labels such as a01, a12, a29 and i15. A high label does not imply that every intervening number is an entry.

This guide covers all 22 published entries plus eight explicitly added foundations, giving 30 numbered items. The additions make trace, j-invariant, field size, subgroup size, cofactor and endomorphisms explicit rather than burying them inside other traits. These are 30 study topics, not 30 independent measures of security or a claim that DiSSECT published 30 tests.

For each topic, separate mathematical structure, a demonstrated security mechanism, implementation dependence, and an unexplained statistical observation. An unusual curve is not thereby a weak curve.
Let E be an elliptic curve over F_q, q=p^m. Write N=#E(F_q), r=ord(G) for a chosen prime-order generator, and h=N/r. Reserve ell for a small auxiliary prime and s for an extension degree.
The central equations are

blocks.pre:
t = q + 1 - N,                  |t| <= 2 sqrt(q)
N_twist = q + 1 + t             (quadratic twist, ordinary setting here)
pi^2 - [t]pi + [q] = 0
D_pi = t^2 - 4q = v^2 d_K      (ordinary curves)
Z[pi] ⊆ End(E) ⊆ O_K
disc(End(E)) = f^2 d_K,         f divides v.

blocks.p: Here pi is q-power Frobenius, d_K is a fundamental imaginary quadratic discriminant, v is the conductor of Z[pi], and f is the conductor of the actual endomorphism ring. v and f need not agree.
For y²=x³+ax+b in characteristic greater than 3,
Delta_E is a field element checking nonsingularity; D_pi is an integer describing Frobenius. They are different discriminants.

traits.title: Field q=p^m and representation
traits.meaning: Specifies coordinate arithmetic. Characteristic, extension degree, subfields and basis affect arithmetic and which mathematical reductions apply. Bit length alone does not establish security.
traits.task: Record p, m, field polynomial/basis, and the smallest field over which the equation is defined. Contrast prime fields with binary extension fields.

traits.title: Group order N and its factorization
traits.meaning: Counts rational points. Pohlig–Hellman separates a cyclic DLP according to prime-power factors of the actual point order. A smooth order is unsuitable even when q is large.
traits.task: Verify N, retain prime factors with exponents, and identify what is proven versus still unfactored. Distinguish N from ord(G).

traits.title: Selected subgroup order r
traits.meaning: Prime r sets the generic classical square-root work scale: roughly sqrt(r) group operations, before constants and usable symmetries.
traits.task: Check r is prime, G is nonzero and [r]G=O. Explain why approximately 256-bit r corresponds to roughly 128-bit generic work.

traits.title: Cofactor h=N/r
traits.meaning: Measures the group outside the selected subgroup. A nontrivial h creates protocol obligations, not an automatic failure of the r-subgroup.
traits.task: State the protocol's subgroup validation or cofactor handling rules. Verify N=hr.

traits.title: Frobenius trace t
traits.meaning: Connects point count, twist, isogeny class and endomorphism algebra. Over F_p, t=1 means N=p, the anomalous case. Ordinarity is equivalent to p not dividing t.
traits.task: Derive N and twist order from t. Label the exact exceptional cases rather than assigning a continuous “weakness score” to t.

traits.title: j-invariant
traits.meaning: Classifies curves up to isomorphism over an algebraic closure. Equal j does not imply isomorphism over the base field; twists are the key example. In characteristic >3, j=0 and 1728 have extra geometric automorphisms.
traits.task: Compare a curve and its twist: same j, usually different orders. Check which automorphisms are actually defined over the working field.

traits.title: Equation discriminant Delta_E
traits.meaning: Nonzero means the equation is nonsingular. Delta_E=0 gives a singular cubic, outside elliptic-curve group assumptions. Its numerical size or integer factorization is not an ECDLP hardness score.
traits.task: Verify nonzero in the field. Change to an isomorphic equation and see why a raw integer lift is representation dependent.

traits.title: Actual endomorphism ring, conductor f and usable maps
traits.meaning: The ordinary endomorphism ring is an order in K. An efficiently evaluable map can help legitimate scalar multiplication; suitable symmetries can also reduce generic search constants. Ring existence does not establish map efficiency.
traits.task: Keep d_K, v, f and explicit maps in separate fields. Record map field of definition, degree, subgroup action and evaluation cost.

traits.title: cofactor / a01
traits.meaning: Group invariant factors over F_(q^s).
traits.task: Write the group as Z/n1 × Z/n2 with n1 dividing n2. Unlike item 4, this describes the whole group, not just one quotient N/r. Check n1*n2=N_s and n1 divides q^s-1.

traits.title: discriminant / a02
traits.meaning: Integer D_pi and its square/fundamental decomposition.
traits.task: Factor D_pi to separate v from d_K. This exposes CM structure; it does not factor a secret scalar. Do not infer the actual ring conductor f from v alone.

traits.title: twist order / a03
traits.meaning: Quadratic-twist cardinality and prime factors.
traits.task: Relevant when an implementation can process twist points, especially x-only arithmetic. Compare r with the twist's largest prime subgroup and review the protocol's accepted inputs. Full point validation changes the relevance.

traits.title: kn fact. / a04
traits.meaning: Factors of kN-1 and kN+1.
traits.task: Treat these as structural observations. For auxiliary-input DLP results, distinguish the subgroup r from N and require the precise additional-input assumptions; smooth r±1 alone does not break ordinary ECDH.

traits.title: torsion extension / a05
traits.meaning: Fields containing some/all ell-torsion.
traits.task: For ell≠p, compare one nonzero torsion point with full E[ell]. The identity is always rational, so “some torsion” must exclude it. Relate extension degrees to Frobenius acting on a two-dimensional vector space.

traits.title: conductor / a06
traits.meaning: Discriminant growth after base extension.
traits.task: Compute D_s/D_1 and separate this trait from f in item 8. It tracks changes in the Frobenius order and rational isogeny structure. Extending the field does not itself change the geometric endomorphism ring.

traits.title: embedding / a07
traits.meaning: Multiplicative order of q modulo r, presented through its complement.
traits.task: Record the actual k=ord_r(q), not just (r-1)/k. Pairing transfer places the DLP in F_(q^k)*; security depends on that finite-field DLP as well as the source group. A universal cutoff on k is insufficient.

traits.title: class number / a08
traits.meaning: Bounds for the imaginary quadratic field class number.
traits.task: Explain ideal classes and their relation to CM/isogenies. Distinguish h(d_K) from h(f²d_K), and both from subgroup cofactor h. Preserve lower/upper bounds rather than reporting them as exact values.

traits.title: small prime order / a12
traits.meaning: Multiplicative order of a small ell modulo N.
traits.task: This is an order in (Z/NZ)*, not the order of a curve point. It is defined only when gcd(ell,N)=1. Relate it to scalar arithmetic; do not identify it with embedding degree unless the base is q.

traits.title: division pol. / a22
traits.meaning: Factorization of an ell-division polynomial.
traits.task: Polynomial factors encode Frobenius orbits of torsion x-coordinates. Compare factor degrees with item 13. Recovering x does not necessarily recover y over the same field; retain the sign distinction.

traits.title: volcano / a23
traits.meaning: Local ell-isogeny graph structure.
traits.task: Relate its levels to ell-adic conductor valuations and splitting in K. Distinguish total volcano depth from the starting curve's level. A readily navigable local graph does not by itself solve a prime-subgroup DLP.

traits.title: isogeny extension / a24
traits.meaning: Fields where some/all degree-ell isogenies are rational.
traits.task: A rational isogeny needs a Frobenius-stable kernel, not individually rational kernel points. Compare stable lines in E[ell] with fixed vectors: this explains why items 13 and 20 differ.

traits.title: trace fact. / a25
traits.meaning: Prime factors of extension traces t_s.
traits.task: Factor signed traces and record zero separately. Smoothness of t_s does not imply smoothness of N_s. Use t_0=2, t_1=t, t_s=t*t_(s-1)-q*t_(s-2) to connect extensions.

traits.title: isogeny neighbors / a28
traits.meaning: Roots of a specialized modular polynomial.
traits.task: Study adjacent j-invariants and compare with items 19–20. Distinct roots, repeated roots, rational kernels and distinct isogenies are not interchangeable counts, especially at special j.

traits.title: q torsion / a29
traits.meaning: Torsion over Q of a chosen coefficient lift.
traits.task: Lifting residues a,b to integers chooses a new curve over Q. This is not a canonical inverse to reduction. Compare different lifts; finite-field ECDLP hardness does not follow from rational torsion size.

traits.title: hamming x / i04
traits.meaning: Counts at specified coordinate Hamming weights.
traits.task: This depends on coordinate representation. Compare equivalent encodings or field bases. A biased point selector or implementation may care about the distribution; the distribution alone is not evidence of key leakage.

traits.title: square 4p-1 / i06
traits.meaning: Squarefree kernels of 4p-1 and 4r-1.
traits.task: Record this as an exploratory arithmetic signature. It is neither N's factorization nor generally the curve's CM discriminant. Explain which integer the paper calls n here: the generator order.

traits.title: pow distance / i07
traits.meaning: Order proximity to binary/word boundaries.
traits.task: Investigate uniform scalar generation and integer representation. Modular reduction of random bits can bias scalars; variable-length processing can leak through an implementation. Neither effect follows solely from proximity to a power of two.

traits.title: multiples x / i08
traits.meaning: x-coordinate of the scalar-divided generator.
traits.task: Interpret G/k as [k^(-1) mod r]G when gcd(k,r)=1. A short coordinate may reveal how G was chosen; it does not reveal an unknown private scalar. Keep generator-specific traits separate from curve invariants.

traits.title: x962 inv. / i13
traits.meaning: a³/b² in the base field.
traits.task: Use it to understand seed-to-coefficient generation. Where defined, j=1728(4u)/(4u+27) for u=a³/b². Thus u and j are algebraically dependent, not independent security signals. Handle b=0 separately.

traits.title: brainpool overlap / i14
traits.meaning: Coefficient bit overlap statistic.
traits.task: Study generation-induced correlations and compare to the specified generation process. A predictable overlap can be expected behavior. It is not a secret-key relation. State bit ordering and the coefficient representation.

traits.title: weierstrass / i15
traits.meaning: Equation coefficients a,b.
traits.task: Small coefficients can simplify arithmetic or reflect deliberate generation. Apply an isomorphism to separate coordinate appearance from curve structure. Small a or b is not a stand-alone weakness.

blocks.p: The basic integer-versus-group distinction matters: a curve point is not an integer with a unique prime factorization. In elliptic-curve index calculus, expressing a point as a sum of factor-base points is a separate decomposition problem. Smoothness of D_pi or t does not establish an easy point decomposition.

blocks.h3: Phase 1 — Build one trustworthy curve record

blocks.p: Cover items 1–7, 9, 11 and 15 first. Start with the worked example and several other tiny curves. Then use published parameters for representative prime-field curves as descriptive examples.

Deliverable: one page per curve with field, equation, generator, exact order relations, factorization status, trace, twist, j, nonsingularity and embedding-degree status. Each entry includes an explanation in words and one equation linking it to another entry.

Completion criteria: all point-count, subgroup and discriminant identities agree; incomplete factorization is visibly incomplete; every security claim names the mathematical or protocol assumption it needs.

blocks.h3: Phase 2 — Connect Frobenius, CM and isogenies

blocks.p: Cover 8, 10, 13–14, 16 and 18–22. Use a tiny ordinary curve so torsion fields and local isogeny graphs can be inspected exactly.

Deliverable: a diagram with Frobenius at the center, branches to point count and twist, to the CM field and orders, and to torsion/isogeny field extensions. Accompany it with a small graph distinguishing volcano depth from a curve's position.
Completion criteria: explain v versus f, field versus order class number, point versus kernel rationality, and polynomial factor degree versus full torsion-point field degree without conflating them.
Cover 17 and 23–30. Compare a curve with an isomorphic equation, another generator of the same subgroup, its quadratic twist and different integer lifts of its coefficients.
Deliverable: a table identifying which traits survive each change. Add a coefficient-generation diagram for X9.62 and Brainpool.

Completion criteria: distinguish a curve invariant, an isogeny invariant, a generator property, a coordinate property and a generation fingerprint. Do not label intended generation structure a weakness.
Revisit 2, 10–12, 14–18, 21 and 25. Construct a concept worksheet with one row per factorization object from the preceding table.

Deliverable: an evidence ledger with the exact integer or polynomial, factors and exponents, remaining cofactor, proof/primality status, field, source and interpretation. For protocol-conditional results, list the additional information required.
Completion criteria: explain why smooth N is different from smooth t, why r±1 requires special care, and why easy polynomial factorization does not itself solve a prime-order DLP.

Use the complete 30-item record for descriptive comparison of public curve parameters. Match field sizes, curve families, subgroup conditions, generation rules and representation. Avoid treating t, N, D_pi and their deterministic transforms as independent observations.

Deliverable: a source-linked comparison report with separate conclusions for established mathematical constraints, implementation questions, expected generation effects and unexplained statistical deviations.

Completion criteria: predeclare comparisons, account for multiple testing, preserve missing values, and confirm unusual observations on independent samples. An outlier alone supports an investigation, not a reduced security-bit claim.

blocks.h3: Phase 6 — Bridge to binary and Koblitz curves

blocks.p: The short-Weierstrass formulas above and the original inventory's ordinary prime-field assumptions cannot simply be copied into characteristic two. Use the correct binary equation and invariants. Mark X9.62/Brainpool-specific tests inapplicable where appropriate.

For a curve defined over F_2 and studied over F_(2^m), separate the 2-power Frobenius sigma from q-power Frobenius pi=sigma^m. On F_(2^m)-rational points, pi is the identity; sigma can act nontrivially because the equation descends to F_2. This distinction explains why the smaller-field Frobenius supplies useful symmetry.

Deliverable: a separate binary-field adapter specification with minimal definition field, trace recurrence, subgroup structure, basis, Frobenius orbit lengths, map field of definition and applicable trait labels. Keep m=83 as the intended high-fidelity descriptive comparison point for the existing research, while making clear that no such evaluation was executed here.
Completion criteria: every formula states its characteristic and ordinarity assumptions. No representation reduction is reported as a measured improvement in relation collection or ECDLP security.

For each curve and trait retain: stable trait ID; source/version; applicability; raw value; normalized display value; defining field and representation; dependencies; exact/bounded/heuristic status; factorization completeness; verification method; mathematical interpretation; protocol assumptions; evidence URL; and whether any security consequence is established or merely a hypothesis.

Do not combine all 30 into a weighted “security score.” Use a structured report. Several traits are deterministic transforms of one another, some are representation dependent, and many have no established monotone connection to DLP hardness.
